paragraphs: Truly God chose (3:33), selected, Adam and Noah and the House of Abraham and the House of ʿImrān, meaning the two of them themselves, above the worlds, by making the prophets of their progeny.
Progeny, one of them from (3:34), the offspring of, another of them; and God is Hearing, Knowing.

Remember when the wife of ʿImrān said (3:35) – she was Ḥannah – when she had grown old and longed for a child, and so prayed to God, and then felt that she was with child: O my Lord, truly I have vowed that I shall make to You what is in my womb, consecrated, set free, devoted wholly, clear of the preoccupations of this world, for the service of Your Holy House; so accept it from me. Truly You are the Hearing of supplication, the Knowing of intentions. And ʿImrān died while she was pregnant.

And when she gave birth to her (3:36), bearing her as a girl, when she had been hoping it would be a boy, since none but boys were consecrated, she said, by way of excuse, My Lord, I have given birth to a female – and God knows best, that is, He is well aware of, what she gave birth to: a parenthetical clause from His speech, Exalted; and in one reading with the tāʾ vowelled with ḍamma{{fn:waḍaʿtu, “what I have given birth to”, making the words part of her own speech.}} – and the male that I asked for is not like the female that I have been given, because he is intended for service, whereas she is not fit for it owing to her weakness, her being ʿawra (something to be screened from view), and what befalls her of menstruation and the like; and I have named her Mary, and I commend her to Your protection, and her offspring, her children, from Satan the accursed, the outcast. And in the ḥadīth{{fn:The ḥadīth alluded to is that related by al-Bukhārī and Muslim: “There is no newborn but Satan touches it when it is born, so that it cries out screaming from his touch, except Mary and her son.”}}.

So her Lord accepted her (3:37), that is, He accepted Mary from her mother, with a goodly acceptance, and made her grow with a goodly growth: He brought her up with a goodly constitution, so that she grew in a day as a newborn grows in a year. Her mother brought her to the rabbis, the custodians of the Holy House (Bayt al-Maqdis), and said: “Here, take this one who was vowed.” They competed for her, because she was the daughter of their leader (imām). Zachariah said: “I have the better right to her, because her maternal aunt is with me.” They said: “No, not until we cast lots.” So they set off – they were twenty-nine – to the river Jordan and cast in their pens, agreeing that the one whose pen held firm in the water and rose to the surface would have the better right to her. Zachariah's pen held firm, so he took her and built for her a chamber in the sanctuary (masjid) with a ladder, which none but he climbed up to her. He would bring her her food, her drink and her oil, and he would find with her the fruit of summer in winter and the fruit of winter in summer, as He, Exalted, said: and Zachariah took charge of her, he took her into his care; and in one reading with the doubled consonant (kaffalahā) and with “Zachariah” in the accusative, both in its lengthened form (Zakariyyāʾ) and in its shortened form (Zakariyyā), the agent being God{{fn:That is, “and He made Zachariah her guardian”.}}. Whenever Zachariah entered upon her in the sanctuary (miḥrāb), the chamber, which is the noblest of sitting-places, he found provision with her. He said: O Mary, whence, from where, have you this? She said – while she was still small – It is from God: He brings it to me from Paradise. Truly God provides for whom He wills without reckoning: ample provision, with no account to render.

There (3:38), that is, when Zachariah saw that, and knew that the One who is able to bring a thing outside its season is able to bring a child in old age – and the people of his house had died out – Zachariah called upon his Lord, when he entered the sanctuary to pray in the depth of the night. He said: My Lord, grant me from Yourself, from Your presence, a goodly offspring, a righteous child; truly You are the Hearer, the Answerer, of supplication.

Then the angels called to him (3:39), that is, Gabriel, while he was standing praying in the sanctuary, that is, the place of worship, that, that is, “saying that”; and in one reading with kasra (inna), with “saying” understood: God gives you good tidings – read with the doubled consonant (yubashshiruka) and without it (yabshuruka) – of John, confirming a Word that is from God, that is, Jesus, that he is the Spirit of God; he was named “a Word” because he was created by the word “Be”; and a lord, one who is followed, and chaste, kept away from women, and a prophet from among the righteous. It is related that he never committed a sin nor ever contemplated one.

He said: My Lord, how (3:40), in what way, shall I have a boy, a child, when old age has overtaken me, that is, I have reached the limit of age, a hundred and twenty years, and my wife is barren, she having reached ninety-eight years? He said: The matter is so, God's creating a boy from the two of you; God does what He wills: nothing renders Him incapable of it. And in order to make manifest this tremendous power, he was inspired to ask the question so that it might be answered with this; and because his soul yearned for the speedy coming of what he had been given tidings of.

He said: My Lord, appoint for me a sign (3:41), that is, a token of my wife's pregnancy. He said: Your sign is that you shall not speak to people: [your sign] for it is that you shall not speak to people, that is, that you refrain from speaking to them – unlike the remembrance of God, Exalted – for three days, that is, together with their nights, except by signal, by gesture; and remember your Lord much, and glorify, pray, in the evening and the early morning, the latter parts of the day and its first parts.

And (3:42) remember when the angels said, that is, Gabriel, O Mary, truly God has chosen you, selected you, and purified you from the touch of men, and chosen you above the women of the worlds, that is, the people of your time.
O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord (3:43), obey Him, and prostrate and bow with those who bow, that is, pray with those who pray.

That (3:44), what has been mentioned of the affair of Zachariah and Mary, is of the tidings of the unseen, the reports of what was hidden from you, which We reveal to you, O Muḥammad; and you were not with them when they cast their pens into the water, drawing lots so that it might become clear to them which of them should take charge of, should bring up, Mary; nor were you with them when they disputed over her guardianship, such that you would know that and report it; rather, you knew it only by way of revelation.

Remember when the angels said (3:45), that is, Gabriel, O Mary, truly God gives you good tidings of a Word from Him, that is, a son, whose name is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary. He addressed her attributing him to her, to draw attention to the fact that she would bear him without a father, since the custom with men is that they are attributed to their fathers; honoured, possessed of standing, in this world, through prophethood, and the Hereafter, through intercession and the highest degrees, and one of those brought near to God.
And he shall speak to people in the cradle (3:46), that is, as an infant, before the time of speech, and in maturity, and shall be one of the righteous.

She said: My Lord, how (3:47), in what way, shall I have a child when no man has touched me, whether by marriage or otherwise? He said: The matter is so, God's creating a child from you without a father; God creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, wills to create it, He only says to it “Be”, and it is, that is, and so it comes to be.
And He will teach him (3:48) – read with nūn (nuʿallimuhu, “We will teach him”) and with yāʾ (yuʿallimuhu) – the Book, writing, and wisdom, and the Torah and the Gospel.

And (3:49) We shall make him a messenger to the Children of Israel, in childhood or after reaching maturity. So Gabriel breathed into the opening of her shift and she conceived, and there befell her what is mentioned in Sūrat Maryam (19:16-34). When God sent him to the Children of Israel he said to them: I am God's messenger to you, in that, that is, “by the fact that”, I have come to you with a sign, a token of my truthfulness, from your Lord; it is that I – in one reading with kasra (innī), as a fresh sentence – create, fashion, for you out of clay the likeness of a bird, something like its form – the kāf{{fn:The particle ka-, “like”, in ka-hayʾati l-ṭayr.}} being a noun standing as the object – then I breathe into it, the pronoun referring to the kāf, and it becomes a bird – in one reading ṭāʾiran – by God's leave, by His will. So he created for them the bat, because it is the most perfectly formed of birds, and it would fly while they watched it, and when it passed out of their sight it would fall down dead. And I heal, I cure, the one born blind, who was born sightless, and the leper – these two are singled out for mention because they are two diseases that defeat the physician, and his mission fell in the age of medicine; and he would heal fifty thousand in a day by supplication, on condition of belief – and I bring the dead to life, by God's leave: He repeated it so as to negate any illusion of divinity in him. So he brought to life ʿĀzar, a friend of his, and the old woman's son, and the tax-collector's daughter, and they lived on and had children born to them; and Shem son of Noah, who died on the spot. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store up, hide away, in your houses, of what I have not witnessed; he would tell a person what he had eaten and what he would eat afterwards. Truly in that which has been mentioned is a sign for you, if you are believers.

And (3:50) I have come to you confirming what was before me, prior to me, of the Torah, and to make lawful to you some of what was forbidden to you in it. So he made lawful to them such fish and birds as have no spur or spine{{fn:ṣīṣiya: a spur, horn or hard protrusion.}}; and it was said that he made all of it lawful, so that “some” has the sense of “all”. And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: he repeated it for emphasis and in order to build upon it: so fear God and obey me in what I command you of affirming God's oneness and obeying Him.
Truly God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This (3:51), which I command you, is a path, a way, that is straight. But they called him a liar and did not believe in him.

And when Jesus perceived (3:52), came to know, disbelief from them, and they wished to kill him, he said: Who will be my helpers, my supporters, going towards God, that I may aid His religion? The disciples said: We are God's helpers, the supporters of His religion. They were the chosen companions of Jesus, the first to believe in him, and they were twelve men; [the name is] from al-ḥawar, which is pure whiteness; and it was said that they were fullers who whitened (yuḥawwirūn) garments, that is, bleached them. We believe, we have faith, in God; and bear witness, O Jesus, that we are submitters.

Our Lord, we believe in what You have sent down (3:53) of the Gospel, and we follow the Messenger, Jesus; so write us down with those who bear witness to You with respect to Your oneness and to Your Messenger with respect to his truthfulness.

He, Exalted, said: And they schemed (3:54), that is, the disbelievers of the Children of Israel against Jesus, when they set over him someone to kill him by stealth; and God schemed against them, in that He cast the likeness of Jesus upon the one who intended to kill him, so that they killed him, and He raised Jesus to heaven; and God is the best of schemers, the most knowing of them in it.

Remember when God said: O Jesus, I am taking you (3:55), seizing you, and raising you to Me from this world without death, and purifying you, removing you far, from those who disbelieve, and placing those who follow you, who affirm your prophethood, of the Muslims and the Christians, above those who disbelieve, namely the Jews, prevailing over them by argument and by the sword, until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is your return, and I shall judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ in the matter of religion.

As for those who disbelieve, I shall punish them with a severe punishment in this world (3:56), through killing, captivity and the poll-tax (jizya), and the Hereafter, through the Fire; and they shall have no helpers to protect them from it.

And as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will pay them in full (3:57) – read with yāʾ (yuwaffīhim) and with nūn (nuwaffīhim, “We will pay them in full”) – their rewards; and God does not love the wrongdoers, that is, He will punish them. It is related that God, Exalted, sent to him a cloud which raised him up, and his mother clung to him and wept, and he said to her: Truly the Resurrection will bring us together. That was on the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) at the Holy House (Bayt al-Maqdis), when he was thirty-three years old; and his mother lived six years after him. The two Shaykhs{{fn:Al-Bukhārī and Muslim.}} related the ḥadīth that he will descend near the Hour and will judge by the law of our Prophet, and will kill the Antichrist (al-Dajjāl) and the swine, break the cross and abolish the poll-tax (jizya). In the ḥadīth of Muslim, he will remain seven years; and in a ḥadīth from Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī, forty years; and he will die and the funeral prayer will be offered over him. So it may be that what is meant is the sum of his sojourn on earth before the raising and after it.

That (3:58), what has been mentioned of the affair of Jesus, We recite it, We relate it, to you, O Muḥammad, of the signs – a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) of the pronoun -hu in natlūhu, its governing element being the demonstrative sense contained in dhālika – and the wise Remembrance, the firmly composed (muḥkam), that is, the Qurʾān.

Truly the likeness of Jesus (3:59), his strange condition, with God is as the likeness of Adam, like his condition, [being] without a father; this is the likening of the strange to what is stranger still, so that it is more decisive against the opponent and more effective upon the soul. He created him, that is, Adam, that is, his mould, of dust, then said to him: Be, a human being, and he was, that is, and he came to be. So too with Jesus: He said to him “Be” – without a father – and he was.
The truth is from your Lord (3:60): the predicate of an elided subject, that is, the affair of Jesus [is the truth from your Lord]; so do not be of the doubters, those who are uncertain about it.

And whoever argues with you (3:61), disputes with you, of the Christians, concerning him after the knowledge that has come to you of his affair, say to them: Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, so that we gather them together, then let us pray humbly, let us plead earnestly in supplication, and invoke the curse of God upon the liars, by saying: O God, curse the liar concerning the affair of Jesus. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) called the delegation of Najrān to this when they argued with him about it, and they said: Let us look into our affair, then we shall come to you. Those of sound judgment among them said: You know well his prophethood, and that no people has ever engaged in mutual imprecation with a prophet without perishing; so make peace with the man and depart. So they came to the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him), who had come out with al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn, Fāṭima and ʿAlī with him, and he said to them: When I supplicate, say “Amen”. But they refused to engage in the mutual cursing, and made terms with him on payment of the poll-tax (jizya). Abū Nuʿaym related it. And from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Had those who were to engage in the mutual imprecation gone out, they would have returned to find neither property nor family. And it is related: Had they gone out, they would have been consumed by fire.

Truly this (3:62), what has been mentioned, is indeed the narrative, the report, that is true, in which there is no doubt; and there is no – min being redundant – god but God; and truly God is indeed the Mighty in His dominion, the Wise in His handiwork.
And if they turn away (3:63), turn aside from belief, then truly God is Knowing of the corrupters, and He will requite them. Here the overt noun is placed in the position of the pronoun.

Say: O People of the Book (3:64), Jews and Christians, come to a word that is equitable – a verbal noun (maṣdar) meaning one whose purport is even – between us and you; it is that we worship none but God, and associate nothing with Him, and that none of us take others as lords besides God, as you have taken the rabbis and the monks. And if they turn away, turn aside from affirming God's oneness, then say, you, to them: Bear witness that we are submitters, affirmers of God's oneness.

So for their breaking (4:155) – mā is redundant, and the bāʾ is causal, attached to an elided verb, that is, “We cursed them because of their breaking” – their covenant, and their disbelief in the signs of God, and their killing the prophets without right, and their saying to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): Our hearts are wrapped, they do not take in your speech. Nay, God has sealed, stamped, them because of their disbelief, so they take in no admonition; so they do not believe, except a few of them, such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his companions.

And for their disbelief (4:156), a second time, in Jesus – the bāʾ is repeated to separate it from what is conjoined to it – and their uttering against Mary a tremendous calumny, in that they accused her of fornication.

And their saying (4:157), boastfully, We killed the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, the messenger of God – according to their claim; that is, on account of the sum of all this We punished them. He, Exalted, said, giving them the lie: And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them: the one killed and crucified – who was one of their own – was made to resemble Jesus, that is, God cast upon him his likeness, so that they thought it was he. And truly those who differ concerning him, that is, concerning Jesus, are in doubt about it, about his killing, for some of them said, when they saw the one who had been killed: The face is the face of Jesus, but the body is not his body, so it is not he; while others said: No, it is he. They have no knowledge of it, of his killing, except the following of conjecture – a disjunctive exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), that is, “but they follow in this the conjecture that they imagined” – and they did not kill him for certain: a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) confirming the negation of the killing.
Nay, God raised him up to Himself; and God is Mighty (4:158) in His dominion, Wise in His handiwork.

And there is not (4:159) – in meaning “not” – of the People of the Book anyone but will surely believe in him, in Jesus, before his death, that is, the death of the person of the Book, when he sees the angels of death, so that his belief does not benefit him; or before the death of Jesus, when he descends near the Hour, as has come in a ḥadīth. And on the Day of Resurrection he, Jesus, shall be a witness against them regarding what they did when he was sent to them.

Remember when God said: O Jesus son of Mary, remember My favour upon you and upon your mother (5:110), by giving thanks for it, when I strengthened you, fortified you, with the Holy Spirit, Gabriel, so that you spoke to people – a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) of the pronoun -ka in ayyadtuka – in the cradle, that is, as an infant, and in maturity: this indicates his descent before the Hour, because he was raised up before reaching maturity, as has preceded in Āl ʿImrān (3:55). And when I taught you the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel; and when you created out of clay the likeness, like the form, of a bird – the kāf being a noun with the sense of “like”, standing as the object – by My leave, then breathed into it, and it became a bird by My leave, by My will; and you healed the one born blind and the leper by My leave; and when you brought forth the dead from their graves, alive, by My leave; and when I restrained the Children of Israel from you, when they intended to kill you, when you came to them with the clear proofs, the miracles, and those of them who disbelieved said: Not – in here meaning mā, “not” – is this, which you have brought, anything but manifest sorcery; and in one reading “a sorcerer” (sāḥir), that is, Jesus.

And when I inspired the disciples (5:111), I commanded them through his tongue, that, that is, “to”, believe in Me and in My messenger, Jesus, they said: We believe in You and in Your messenger, and bear witness that we are submitters.

Remember when the disciples said: O Jesus son of Mary, can (5:112), that is, will He do it, your Lord – in one reading with the tāʾ and what follows it in the accusative (hal tastaṭīʿu rabbaka), that is, “are you able to ask Him” – send down to us a table from heaven? He said, Jesus, to them: Fear God in proposing signs, if you are believers.

They said: We wish (5:113) to ask for it in order that we may eat of it and that there may be at rest, be tranquil, our hearts, through an increase of certainty, and that we may know, grow in knowledge, that – the lightened form (an), that is, “that you” – you have told us the truth in claiming prophethood, and that we may be witnesses to it.

Jesus son of Mary said: O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, that it may be for us (5:114), that is, the day of its descent, a festival, which we shall honour and ennoble, for the first of us – a substitute (badal) for “for us”, with the preposition repeated – and the last of us, those who come after us, and a sign from You of Your power and my prophethood; and provide for us, with it, for You are the best of providers.

God said (5:115), answering him: I am going to send it down – read without doubling (munziluhā) and with doubling (munazziluhā) – to you; but whoever of you disbelieves after, that is, after its descent, I shall punish him with a punishment with which I do not punish anyone of the worlds. So the angels brought it down from heaven, bearing seven loaves and seven fish, and they ate of it until they were satisfied; this was said by Ibn ʿAbbās. And in a ḥadīth: the table was sent down from heaven with bread and meat, and they were commanded not to betray the trust nor to store up for the morrow; but they betrayed it and stored up, and so they were transformed into apes and swine.

And (5:116) remember when God said, that is, will say, to Jesus on the Day of Resurrection, in rebuke of his people: O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides God? He said, Jesus – and he had been made to tremble – Glory be to You, declaring You far above what does not befit You, such as a partner or otherwise; it is not, it is not fitting, for me to say what I have no right to – [bi-ḥaqq] is the predicate of laysa, and lī is for clarification – had I said it, You would have known it. You know what I hide within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself, that is, what You keep hidden of the things You know. Truly You are the Knower of the unseen things.

I said to them nothing except what You commanded me (5:117), which is: Worship God, my Lord and your Lord. And I was a witness over them, a watcher, restraining them from what they say, as long as I remained among them; but when You took me, seized me by raising me to heaven, You were the Watcher over them, the Keeper of their deeds; and You are over all things – of my speech to them and their speech after me and other than that – a Witness, aware of it and knowing it.

If You punish them (5:118), that is, those of them who persisted in disbelief, they are Your servants, and You are their Owner, disposing of them as You will, with no objection to be raised against You; and if You forgive them, that is, those of them who believed, then truly You are the Mighty, the One who prevails in His affair, the Wise in His handiwork.

God said: This (5:119), that is, the Day of Resurrection, is the day when there shall benefit the truthful in this world, such as Jesus, their truthfulness, because it is the Day of Recompense; and those who were liars in this world will not be benefited by their truthfulness on it, such as the disbelievers, when they believe upon seeing the punishment. They shall have gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. God is well pleased with them for their obedience to Him, and they are well pleased with Him for His reward. That is the great triumph. And those who were liars in this world will not be benefited by their truthfulness on it, such as the disbelievers, when they believe upon seeing the punishment.

To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth (5:120) – the storehouses of rain, vegetation, provision and other things – and whatever is in them: He used mā, giving predominance to the non-rational; and He has power over all things, among which is the rewarding of the truthful and the punishing of the liar.

And mention in the Book (19:16), the Qurʾān, Mary, that is, her story, when, at the time when, she withdrew from her family to an eastern place, that is, she secluded herself in a place towards the east of the house.

And she took a screen apart from them (19:17): she let down a curtain to conceal herself behind, so as to delouse her head, or her clothes, or to wash herself after her menses. Then We sent to her Our Spirit, Gabriel, and he took on for her – after she had put on her clothes – the likeness of a well-proportioned man, perfect in form.
She said: I seek refuge in the All-Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing (19:18), so that you will desist from me on account of my seeking refuge.
He said: I am only the messenger of your Lord, to grant you a boy who is pure (19:19), through prophethood.
She said: How shall I have a boy when no man has touched me (19:20), by marriage, nor have I been unchaste, a fornicatress?

He said (19:21), Gabriel: The matter is so, God's creating a boy from you without a father; your Lord has said: It is easy for Me, that is, by Gabriel's breathing into you at My command, so that you conceive him. And since what has been mentioned has the sense of a cause, the following is conjoined to it: and so that We may make him a sign for people, of Our power, and a mercy from Us for whoever believes in him; and it was, his creation, a matter decreed, in My knowledge. So Gabriel breathed into the opening of her shift, and she felt the conception in her womb, already formed.
So she conceived him, and she withdrew (19:22), retired, with him to a far place, distant from her family.

Then there drove her (19:23), brought her, the pangs of childbirth, the pain of labour, to the trunk of the palm-tree, so that she might lean upon it; and she gave birth – the conception, the formation and the birth all took place within a single hour. She said: O – for calling attention – would that I had died before this affair, and been a thing forgotten, consigned to oblivion, something abandoned, neither known nor remembered.
Then he called to her from beneath her (19:24), that is, Gabriel, who was lower down than she: Do not grieve; your Lord has placed beneath you a rivulet, a stream of water which had dried up.

And shake towards you the trunk of the palm-tree (19:25) – it was withered, and the bāʾ is redundant – it will drop – originally with two tāʾs (tatasāqaṭ), the second changed into sīn and assimilated into the sīn; in one reading it is left out – upon you dates, a specification (tamyīz), fresh and ripe, its adjective.

So eat (19:26) of the fresh dates, and drink of the rivulet, and be comforted of eye by the child – a specification (tamyīz) transposed from the subject, that is, “so that your eye be comforted by him”, meaning that it be at rest and not look towards anything else. And if – here the nūn of the conditional in is assimilated into the redundant mā – you should see – from it the final radical and the middle radical of the verb have been elided, the vowel of the latter transferred to the rāʾ, and the yāʾ of the pronoun given a kasra because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters – any human being, who then asks you about your child, say: I have vowed to the All-Merciful a fast, that is, an abstention from speaking about his affair and other matters with human beings, as is shown by: so I shall not speak today to any human, that is, after this.

Then she brought him to her people, carrying him (19:27) – a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) – and they saw him. They said: O Mary, you have indeed done a monstrous thing, a grave thing, in that you have brought a child without a father.

O sister of Aaron (19:28) – he was a righteous man; that is, O you who are like him in chastity – your father was not an evil man, that is, a fornicator, nor was your mother unchaste, that is, a fornicatress; so from where have you this child?
Then she pointed (19:29), to them, to him, [as if to say] speak to him. They said: How shall we speak to one who is, that is, who is found, in the cradle, a child?
He said: I am the servant of God. He has given me the Book (19:30), that is, the Gospel, and made me a prophet.

And He has made me blessed wherever I may be (19:31), that is, greatly beneficial to people – an announcement of what had been decreed for him – and has enjoined upon me prayer and alms, He commanded me with them both, as long as I live.
And dutiful towards my mother (19:32) – in the accusative, governed by an implied “He has made me” – and He has not made me arrogant, self-aggrandising, wretched, disobedient to his Lord.
And peace (19:33), from God, be upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive. What was said earlier regarding the lord John is said of this too.

He, Exalted, said: That is Jesus son of Mary, the word of truth (19:34) – in the nominative, the predicate of an implied subject, that is, “[this is] the word of the son of Mary”; and in the accusative, with “I say” implied, the meaning being “the true word” – concerning which they are in doubt, from mirya, that is, they doubt; they are the Christians, who said that Jesus is the son of God. They lied.

It is not for God to take any son. Glory be to Him (19:35), declaring Him far above that. When He decrees a matter, that is, wills to bring it into being, He only says to it “Be”, and it is – in the nominative (fa-yakūnu), with “he” implied; and in the accusative (fa-yakūna), with an implied. And among such is the creation of Jesus without a father.

And truly God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him (19:36) – with anna taking fatḥa, with “remember” implied; and with kasra (inna), with “say” implied, as is shown by I said to them nothing except what You commanded me: Worship God, my Lord and your Lord (5:117). This, what has been mentioned, is a path, a way, that is straight, leading to Paradise.

But the factions differed among themselves (19:37), that is, the Christians, concerning Jesus: is he the son of God, or a god alongside Him, or the third of three? So woe, severity of punishment, to those who disbelieve in what has been mentioned and in other things, from the witnessing of a tremendous day, that is, being present at the Day of Resurrection and its terrors.

And (21:91) remember Mary, she who guarded her chastity, protected it from being touched, so We breathed into her of Our Spirit, that is, Gabriel, in that he breathed into the opening of her shift and she conceived Jesus, and We made her and her son a sign for the worlds, mankind, the jinn and the angels, in that she bore him without a male.

And We made the son of Mary (23:50), Jesus, and his mother a sign – He did not say “two signs”, because the sign in the two of them is one: his birth without a male – and We gave them refuge on a height, an elevated place, which is the Holy House (Bayt al-Maqdis), or Damascus, or Palestine – various opinions – possessed of a settled place, that is, level, on which its inhabitants settle, and a flowing spring, that is, running water, visible, which the eyes see.

And when was struck (43:57), was set forth, the son of Mary as an example – when His words, Exalted, came down: You and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell (21:98), the idolaters said: We are content that our gods should be with Jesus, for he was worshipped besides God – behold, your people, that is, the idolaters, at it, at the example, cry out, laugh in delight at what they heard.

And they said: Are our gods better, or he (43:58), that is, Jesus? So we are content for our gods to be with him. They did not strike it, that is, the example, for you except in argument, contention by falsehood, for they knew that mā is for the non-rational and so does not include Jesus (peace be upon him). Nay, but they are a contentious people, vehement in dispute.

He is not (43:59), Jesus is not, but a servant on whom We bestowed favour, through prophethood, and We made him, by his coming into being without a father, an example for the Children of Israel, that is, like a proverb, on account of his strangeness, by which the power of God, Exalted, over whatever He wills is inferred.
And had We willed, We would have made from you (43:60), in your stead, angels in the earth to succeed, by destroying you.

And truly he (43:61), that is, Jesus, is a sign of the Hour, which is known by his descent, so do not doubt it, that is, be not in doubt about it – the nūn of the indicative has been elided from it for the jussive, and the wāw of the pronoun because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters – and say to them: follow me in affirming God's oneness. This, which I command you, is a path, a way, that is straight.
And let him not turn you away (43:62), divert you from the religion of God, Satan; truly he is to you a manifest enemy, of evident enmity.

And when Jesus came with the clear proofs (43:63), with the miracles and the laws, he said: I have come to you with wisdom, with prophethood and the laws of the Gospel, and to make clear to you some of that over which you differ of the rulings of the Torah, in the matter of religion and otherwise; and he made clear to them the matter of religion. So fear God and obey me.
Truly God, He is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a path (43:64), a way, that is straight.

But the factions differed among themselves (43:65) concerning Jesus: is he God, or the son of God, or the third of three? So woe, a word of punishment, to those who do wrong, who disbelieve by what they said concerning Jesus, from the punishment of a painful day, one that causes pain.

Then We sent following in their footsteps Our messengers, and We sent following Jesus son of Mary, and gave him the Gospel, and placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy, and monasticism (57:27) – this is the renouncing of women and the taking up of hermit-cells – which they innovated, of their own accord; We did not prescribe it for them, We did not command them with it, except – but they did it – seeking the good pleasure, the approval, of God; but they did not observe it with its due observance, since many of them abandoned it and disbelieved in the religion of Jesus and entered into the religion of their king; while many of them remained upon the religion of Jesus and believed in our Prophet. So We gave those of them who believed, in him, their reward; but many of them are transgressors.

And (61:6) remember when Jesus son of Mary said: O Children of Israel – he did not say “O my people”, because he had no kinship among them – I am the messenger of God to you, confirming what was before me, prior to me, of the Torah, and bringing good tidings of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Aḥmad. He, Exalted, said: But when he came to them, when Aḥmad came to the disbelievers, with the clear proofs, the signs and tokens, they said: This, that is, the bringing of it, is sorcery – in one reading “a sorcerer” (sāḥir), that is, the one bringing it – manifest, evident.
